overview:
## Registry-derived inline-shell wrapper classification — Difficulty: 3/5

This change removes the hand-maintained `INLINE_SHELL_WRAPPERS` set in the engine and replaces it with shell-ast 0.8.0's registry-derived `isShellInterpreter(wrapper)` predicate, so the SA-02 opaque-inline-shell escalation can no longer drift from shell-ast's wrapper registry and now covers `runuser -c "$DYN"` and `su -c "$DYN"` that the hand-set under-covered. The dependency bumps from `^0.7.0` to `^0.8.0`. Because shell-ast 0.8.0 also ships six more tools in its built-in `GLOBAL_VALUE_FLAGS` table (including `terraform`), the global-flags pass-through tests re-point their fixtures from `terraform` to still-unregistered tools (`kustomize`, `helm`) so the registration path stays genuinely load-bearing rather than passing trivially.

This is a security-adjacent boundary: the predicate decides whether a dynamic-bodied wrapper (`bash -c "$X"`, `runuser -c "$EVIL"`) gets escalated under the uncertainty policy or silently falls through. Widening the matched set is fail-closed (more escalation), but any narrowing relative to the old set would open a deny-bypass.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["unwrap chain layer u"] --> B{"u.kind === wrapped-opaque?"}
  B -->|"no"| E["wrapped-script / other paths"]
  B -->|"yes"| C{"isShellInterpreter(u.wrapper)?"}
  C -->|"no (sudo, env, timeout)"| D["not an inline-shell body — skip"]
  C -->|"yes (bash, sh, eval, su, runuser, ...)"| F["escalate uncertaintyDecision"]
  F --> G{"esc.kind === deny?"}
  G -->|"yes"| H["return terminal deny, drop warning/note"]
  G -->|"ask"| I["terminal ??= esc, continue"]
  class C,F chg
  classDef chg fill:#d6ffd9,stroke:#1a7f37,color:#111
```

Riskiest area to watch: whether `isShellInterpreter` is exactly equivalent-or-superset to the deleted set for every previously-escalated interpreter (`bash`/`sh`/`zsh`/`ksh`/`mksh`/`dash`/`ash`/`eval`/`su`/`runuser`) and still excludes every non-shell wrapper (`sudo`/`gosu`/`exec`/`env`/`xargs`/`timeout`) — a regression either direction is a silent escalation change.

## Strict review

### Issues outside the diff

- **`tests/engine/opaque-inline-shell.test.ts:51`** — Add regression tests pinning that the non-shell wrappers the engine change names as out-of-scope (`env "$X"`, `timeout "$X"`, `gosu "$X"`, `exec "$X"`) do NOT escalate. The refactor at src/engine/index.ts:614 replaced the locally-controlled INLINE_SHELL_WRAPPERS set with the external `isShellInterpreter` predicate, so the only thing now preventing these wrappers from escalating is the dependency's classification. The suite covers only the `sudo $X` non-escalation case; the other named non-shell wrappers from the deleted comment and CHANGELOG equivalence claim have no test, so a future shell-ast change classifying e.g. `env` as a shell interpreter would silently begin escalating with nothing red.

Inline comments mark required changes. Requesting changes until every thread is resolved.
